informal_statement: An element is a loop if and only if its singleton set is a circuit.
informal_proof:
First, suppose that an element \( a \) is a loop. By definition, this means \( a \) is an edge that connects a vertex to itself, effectively forming a closed path with just that one edge. Therefore, the set containing only \( a \) forms a circuit, as it satisfies the condition of being a closed path without repeating edges. Hence, if \( a \) is a loop, then the singleton set \( \{a\} \) is a circuit.

Conversely, assume that the singleton set \( \{a\} \) is a circuit. By the definition of a circuit, it must form a closed path without repeating edges. Since the set contains only one edge \( a \), the only way for it to form a closed path is if \( a \) connects a vertex to itself, making \( a \) a loop. Therefore, if \( \{a\} \) is a circuit, then \( a \) must be a loop.

Thus, we have shown both directions: an element is a loop if and only if its singleton set is a circuit.

id.name: Matroid.loop_iff_circuit
id.content:
/-- An element is a loop iff its singleton set is a circuit. -/
lemma Matroid.loop_iff_circuit (M : Matroid α) {a : α} :
    M.Loop a ↔ M.Circuit {a} :=
  ⟨
    fun ha => ⟨
      ha.right,
      fun _ hM hMa => (Set.subset_singleton_iff_eq.→ hMa).casesOn
        (· ▸ hM |>.not_indep M.empty_indep |>.elim)
        (·.symm.subset)
      ⟩,
    fun ha => ⟨ha.left.right rfl, ha.dep⟩
  ⟩

import Mathlib.Data.Matroid.Basic
import Seymour.Matroid.Notions.Circuit


variable {α : Type}

/-- Loop is an element of the ground set that is not independent when viewed as a singleton set. -/
def Matroid.Loop (M : Matroid α) (a : α) : Prop :=
  a ∈ M.E ∧ M.Dep {a}

/-- An element is a loop iff its singleton set is a circuit. -/
lemma Matroid.loop_iff_circuit (M : Matroid α) {a : α} :
    M.Loop a ↔ M.Circuit {a} :=
  ⟨
    fun ha => ⟨
      ha.right,
      fun _ hM hMa => (Set.subset_singleton_iff_eq.→ hMa).casesOn
        (· ▸ hM |>.not_indep M.empty_indep |>.elim)
        (·.symm.subset)
      ⟩,
    fun ha => ⟨ha.left.right rfl, ha.dep⟩
  ⟩

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem subset_singleton_iff_eq {s : Set α} {x : α} : s ⊆ {x} ↔ s = ∅ ∨ s = {x} := by
  obtain rfl | hs := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
  · exact ⟨fun _ => Or.inl rfl, fun _ => empty_subset _⟩
  · simp [eq_singleton_iff_nonempty_unique_mem, hs, hs.ne_empty]
